note: Recipes are written for family cooking during the Dormition Fast. Where a dish is named after a traditional preparation but adapted (for example, made without oil), it is labelled 'inspired by'.

recipes.name: Lentil soup (fakes)
directions: Water-sauté the onion, garlic and carrot in a dry pot with a splash of water, adding more water as it sticks, about 8 minutes.
Add lentils, bay leaf, oregano, tomato paste and water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 30–35 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Remove the bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the vinegar off the heat. Taste and add more.
recipes.oilFree: As written, this recipe uses no oil. On a wine-and-oil day, sauté in 3 tbsp olive oil instead of water and finish each bowl with a drizzle.
recipes.childFriendly: Blend half the soup smooth and serve with bread for dipping.
recipes.batch: Doubles well. Freezes for 3 months.
recipes.leftovers: Thin with water for soup, or reduce and serve over rice.
recipes.allergens: None common. Check your bread separately.

recipes.name: Mushroom barley soup
directions: Dry-sear the mushrooms in a hot pot without oil until they release their liquid and it evaporates, 8–10 minutes.
Add onion, carrot, celery and garlic with a splash of broth. Cook 5 minutes.
Add barley, thyme, soy sauce and broth. Bring to a boil.
Simmer covered 40 minutes until the barley is tender.
Season and finish with parsley.
recipes.oilFree: Written oil-free. The dry-sear is what builds the flavour — do not rush it.
recipes.childFriendly: Chop the mushrooms small so they disappear into the broth.
recipes.batch: Barley thickens as it sits; add broth when reheating.
recipes.leftovers: Serve thickened over baked potatoes.
recipes.allergens: Gluten (barley, soy sauce). Use tamari and swap barley for rice if needed.

recipes.name: White bean and tomato soup
ingredients: 3 cups cooked cannellini beans, or 2 cans, drained
directions: Water-sauté the onion and garlic until soft, 6 minutes.
Add tomatoes, herbs and half the beans. Simmer 15 minutes.
Blend the soup smooth with an immersion blender.
Stir in the remaining whole beans and the water. Simmer 10 minutes.
Season well. Serve with bread.
recipes.oilFree: Written oil-free. On an oil day, finish with olive oil and cracked pepper.
recipes.childFriendly: Blend completely smooth and call it tomato soup.
recipes.batch: Triples easily for a parish meal.
recipes.leftovers: Toss with pasta and it becomes a sauce.

recipes.name: Three-bean chili
ingredients: 1 can each black beans, kidney beans and pinto beans, drained
directions: Water-sauté onion, pepper and garlic 8 minutes.
Add the spices and tomato paste. Stir 1 minute to bloom them.
Add tomatoes, beans and water. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
Season with salt and serve with lime.
recipes.oilFree: Written oil-free.
recipes.childFriendly: Halve the chili powder and serve over rice with tortilla chips.
recipes.batch: The best batch-cook of the fast. Slow cooker: 6 hours on low. Instant Pot: 12 minutes high pressure, natural release.
recipes.leftovers: Fills burritos, tops baked potatoes, thins into soup.

recipes.name: Mujadara, oil-free
directions: Simmer the lentils in 4 cups water for 20 minutes until just tender. Do not drain.
Meanwhile, cook the sliced onions in a dry heavy skillet over medium heat, stirring often. They will stick — deglaze with a tablespoon of water each time. Continue 25–30 minutes until deeply browned.
Add rice, cumin, cinnamon, salt and the remaining water to the lentils.
Cover and cook 18 minutes on low, then rest off heat 10 minutes.
Fold in most of the onions, scatter the rest on top, and serve with lemon.
recipes.oilFree: This is an oil-free adaptation. Traditional mujadara fries the onions in a generous amount of olive oil — do that on a wine-and-oil day.
recipes.childFriendly: Serve with cucumber and tomato on the side.
recipes.batch: Makes excellent lunches. The onions can be browned a day ahead.
recipes.leftovers: Pan-crisp in a dry skillet and top with salad.

recipes.name: Red lentil dal
directions: Water-sauté onion, ginger and garlic 6 minutes.
Add the dry spices and stir 30 seconds.
Add lentils, tomatoes and water. Bring to a boil.
Simmer 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils collapse.
Season with salt and lemon. Finish with cilantro. Serve over rice.
recipes.oilFree: Written oil-free. On an oil day, bloom the spices in hot oil first — it is noticeably better.
recipes.childFriendly: Leave out the chili flakes and serve with plain rice.
recipes.batch: Instant Pot: 6 minutes high pressure. Doubles well.
recipes.leftovers: Thickens overnight; loosen with water.

recipes.name: Peppers stuffed with rice and lentils
ingredients: 6 bell peppers, tops cut off and seeded
directions: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Water-sauté onion and garlic 6 minutes. Stir in tomato paste.
Off the heat, mix in rice, lentils, herbs, salt and pepper.
Fill the peppers about three-quarters full — the rice expands. Replace the tops.
Stand them in a baking dish, pour 2 cups water around them, cover with foil.
Bake 50 minutes covered, then 10 minutes uncovered.
recipes.oilFree: Written oil-free. On an oil day, drizzle olive oil over the peppers before baking.
recipes.childFriendly: Use small sweet peppers and let children fill them.
recipes.batch: Assemble a day ahead and refrigerate unbaked.
recipes.leftovers: Chop and fold into soup or a grain bowl.

recipes.name: Briam
directions: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Toss all the vegetables with the olive oil, garlic, herbs, salt and pepper in a large roasting pan.
Spread evenly. Add 1/2 cup water.
Bake 45 minutes, then stir gently.
Bake another 25–30 minutes until the edges caramelise and the potatoes are tender.
Rest 15 minutes before serving. Briam is meant to be eaten warm, not hot.
recipes.oilFree: Not suitable — olive oil is the dish. Make it on a Saturday or Sunday.
recipes.childFriendly: Cut everything small and serve with bread.
recipes.batch: Better the next day. Doubles across two pans.
recipes.leftovers: Excellent cold, in a pita, or stirred into pasta.

recipes.name: Fasolakia
directions: Warm the olive oil in a wide pot. Cook the onion and garlic gently 8 minutes.
Add tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Add beans, potatoes, water, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer 35 minutes until the beans are very soft — this is not a crisp-tender dish.
Stir in parsley. Serve warm with bread.
recipes.oilFree: Not suitable as written; the olive oil is essential.
recipes.childFriendly: Very mild. Serve with bread for dipping.
recipes.batch: Doubles well; reheats better than most vegetable dishes.
recipes.leftovers: Serve cold as a salad with lemon.

recipes.name: Falafel
ingredients: 2 cups dried chickpeas, soaked 12 hours and drained — do not use canned
Olive oil for frying or brushing
directions: Pulse the drained soaked chickpeas with onion, garlic and herbs in a food processor until it resembles coarse sand. Do not purée.
Mix in the spices, salt, baking soda and flour. Rest 30 minutes in the fridge.
Shape into small patties.
Shallow-fry in olive oil 3 minutes per side, or brush with oil and bake at 400°F for 20 minutes, turning once.
Serve in pita with tahini sauce, tomato and cucumber.
recipes.oilFree: Baked falafel still needs a brush of oil to hold together and brown — make it on a Saturday or Sunday.
recipes.childFriendly: Bake rather than fry, and serve with plain tahini thinned with lemon and water.
recipes.batch: Freeze the raw shaped patties on a tray, then bag.
recipes.leftovers: Crumble over a grain bowl.

recipes.name: Greek lemon potatoes
directions: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Toss everything together in a roasting pan. The potatoes should sit in liquid.
Bake 45 minutes.
Turn the potatoes, then bake 20–25 minutes more until the liquid has mostly gone and the edges are golden.
Squeeze over more lemon before serving.
recipes.oilFree: Not suitable — the oil and lemon together make the dish.
recipes.childFriendly: Universally popular. Reduce the garlic if needed.
recipes.batch: The obvious side for the August 6 celebration meal.
recipes.leftovers: Crisp in a hot dry pan.

recipes.name: Vegetable tagine with chickpeas
directions: Water-sauté onion and garlic 6 minutes.
Add the spices and stir 30 seconds.
Add all remaining ingredients except cilantro. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer 35 minutes until the squash is tender.
Season, finish with cilantro, serve over couscous.
recipes.oilFree: Written oil-free.
recipes.childFriendly: The apricots make it sweet; most children take to it.
recipes.batch: Slow cooker: 6 hours low. Instant Pot: 10 minutes high pressure.
recipes.leftovers: Excellent over baked potatoes.

recipes.name: Oil-free baked oatmeal
ingredients: 2.5 cups water or oat drink with no added oil
directions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Line an 8x11 dish with parchment.
Whisk applesauce, syrup, liquid, cinnamon, baking powder and salt.
Stir in oats, apples and raisins.
Spread in the dish and bake 40 minutes until set and golden at the edges.
Cool 10 minutes before cutting.
recipes.oilFree: Written oil-free — the applesauce replaces the fat.
recipes.childFriendly: Cut into squares for a portable breakfast.
recipes.batch: Makes a week of breakfasts. Reheat portions with a splash of water.
recipes.leftovers: Eat cold, or warm with fruit.
recipes.allergens: Oats — use certified gluten-free if needed.

recipes.name: Summer fruit crisp
ingredients: 6 cups sliced peaches, plums or berries
directions: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Toss the fruit with sugar, cornstarch and cinnamon. Spread in a baking dish.
Mix oats, flour, brown sugar, salt and applesauce until crumbly.
Scatter over the fruit.
Bake 40 minutes until bubbling at the edges. Cool 20 minutes.
recipes.oilFree: Written oil-free. On an oil day, swap the applesauce for 1/3 cup olive oil — richer and crisper.
recipes.childFriendly: Let children scatter the topping.
recipes.batch: Doubles into a large pan for a parish gathering.
recipes.leftovers: Eat cold for breakfast without apology.

recipes.name: Greek baked fish with lemon and herbs
ingredients: 2.5 lb firm white fish fillets, or 2 whole fish, cleaned
Juice of 2 lemons, plus 1 lemon sliced
directions: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Scatter onion, garlic and half the tomatoes in a baking dish. Drizzle with half the oil.
Lay the fish on top. Season well.
Cover with the remaining tomatoes, lemon slices, parsley and oregano.
Pour over the lemon juice, wine and remaining oil.
Bake 30–35 minutes, basting once, until the fish flakes. Rest 5 minutes.
Serve with lemon potatoes and bread.
recipes.oilFree: Not applicable — August 6 is designated Fish, Oil and Wine Allowed.
recipes.childFriendly: Use skinless fillets and serve plain portions before adding the tomato and herbs.
recipes.batch: Scales to a large pan for the parish hall. Bake in two dishes rather than crowding one.
recipes.leftovers: Flake into a salad with white beans.
recipes.allergens: Fish. Wine — substitute broth and extra lemon if you prefer.

recipes.name: Chickpea and spinach stew
directions: Water-sauté the onion and garlic 6 minutes.
Add paprika and cumin; stir 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, chickpeas and broth. Simmer 12 minutes.
Stir in the bread if using, then the spinach until wilted.
Season with salt and a good splash of vinegar off the heat.
recipes.oilFree: Written oil-free. On an oil day, fry the bread in olive oil first — that is the traditional Andalusian move this is inspired by.
recipes.childFriendly: Blend half smooth; serve with rice.
recipes.batch: Doubles well; better next day.
recipes.leftovers: Excellent over baked potatoes.

recipes.name: Rice and black bean bowls
ingredients: 2 cans black beans with their liquid
Salsa, corn, shredded lettuce, cilantro to build
directions: Cook the rice.
Water-sauté onion and garlic 6 minutes; add the spices for 30 seconds.
Add the beans and their liquid; simmer 10 minutes and mash a few against the pot.
Season with salt and one lime's juice.
Set out bowls and toppings; everyone builds their own.
recipes.oilFree: Written oil-free.
recipes.childFriendly: The build-your-own format is the point — children eat what they assemble.
recipes.batch: Beans keep 5 days and improve.
recipes.leftovers: Wrap in a tortilla for lunch.

recipes.name: Pasta with tomato sauce
ingredients: 2 cans (28 oz total) whole peeled tomatoes
1 tsp dried basil or a handful fresh
directions: Simmer tomatoes, onion halves, garlic, basil, sugar and salt 25 minutes, crushing the tomatoes as they soften.
Remove the onion. Blend smooth or leave rustic.
Cook the pasta very al dente; finish it in the sauce with a ladle of pasta water for 2 minutes.
Taste; it will want more salt than you think.
recipes.oilFree: Written oil-free — the onion-in, onion-out trick replaces the soffritto. On an oil day, start with 1/3 cup olive oil and it becomes a different, richer sauce.
recipes.childFriendly: The house default. Blend fully smooth.
recipes.batch: Sauce freezes 3 months; make triple.
recipes.leftovers: Bake leftover pasta with breadcrumbs on top.

recipes.name: Mediterranean grain bowl
directions: Cook the grain; cool slightly.
Whisk oil, lemon, oregano, salt and pepper.
Toss everything with the dressing.
Rest 10 minutes so the grain drinks the dressing. Serve at room temperature.
recipes.oilFree: On a strict day, drop the oil and double the lemon with 2 tbsp of the chickpea liquid whisked in — honestly good, differently.
recipes.childFriendly: Serve the parts unmixed.
recipes.batch: Keeps 3 days dressed; the classic make-Sunday-eat-Tuesday lunch.
recipes.leftovers: Stuff into pita.
recipes.allergens: Gluten (bulgur, farro); sesame if using hummus.

recipes.name: Spanakorizo — spinach and rice
ingredients: 2 tbsp tomato paste (optional, for the red version)
directions: Warm the oil; cook onion and scallions gently 8 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste if using, then the rice for 1 minute.
Add water and salt; simmer covered 12 minutes.
Pile the spinach on top, cover, and cook 8 minutes more; stir through with the dill.
Rest 10 minutes off the heat. Finish with lemon.
recipes.oilFree: The oil is structural here; on strict days make the rice-and-greens soup version with broth instead.
recipes.childFriendly: Mild and soft; a good first Greek dish for children.
recipes.batch: Best fresh; keeps 2 days.
recipes.leftovers: Add broth and it becomes soup.
